The data above is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ compute $P(Z>0.64).$ Use the table above and do not round your answer.

$P(Z>0.64)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/d59151ff19329029e209bd271c992c775777939ed0a670c4ce73e0985328bf6b.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>0.64).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/a16528d20a4a8182b6f5898def6f1337450b7fe6d0305644ed214237716d47ae.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<-0.64).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/eb2863fc4ff489cf258e6d80c44efc3c4d6ac7b08be5c71260feb8813934bc6d.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>0.64)=P(Z<-0.64)=Φ(-0.64)=0.2611.
$$
